title: Mechanisms of enhanced or impaired DNA target selectivity driven by protein dimerization.
authors: Sang, Mankun; Au, Gabriel; Johnson, Margaret E
one_liner_zh: 该文通过随机模拟与质量作用模型研究蛋白二聚化对DNA靶标选择性和驻留时间的影响，属于广义蛋白-DNA互作动态机制建模，方法可迁移至TF-DNA体系，但非直接聚焦TF-DNA结合位点预测。
abstract: Successful DNA transcription demands coordination between proteins that bind DNA while simultaneously binding to one another to form dimers or higher-order complexes. For proteins with numerous DNA targets throughout the genome, measurements that report on their dwell time or occupancy thus represent a convolution over a population interacting with specific DNA, nonspecific DNA, or protein partners on DNA. Dimerization is known to add contacts that can help a protein monomer to stably bind DNA. However, we show here that dimerization can also impair measured dwell times and occupancy on target sequences because the population redistributes across DNA. We combine spatial stochastic simulations of pairwise reversible reactions between proteins and DNA with mass-action kinetic models and theory to isolate the role of reversible dimerization on observed DNA dwell times, occupancy, and spatial distribution of proteins on DNA. Three key themes emerge: (i) Protein-protein interactions, in addition to protein-DNA interactions, can localize a protein to DNA, and rates of (un)binding can thus widely tune dwell times. (ii) Dimensional reduction achieved through nonspecific binding and subsequent 1D diffusion controls the order of magnitude of enhancements despite nucleosome barriers. (iii) Dimerization enhances selectivity for locally clustered targets and often impairs binding to widely spaced targets by sequestration. Compared with ChIP-seq data, our model explains how the distribution of the essential GAGA factor monomer throughout the genome is highly selective for clustered targets due to protein interactions. This model framework predicts when even weak dimerization can redistribute and stabilize proteins on DNA as a necessary part of transcription.
abstract_zh: 成功的DNA转录需要DNA结合蛋白之间的协调，这些蛋白在结合DNA的同时彼此结合形成二聚体或高阶复合物。对于基因组中拥有众多DNA靶标的蛋白质，测量其停留时间或占据率的实验，实际上是对与特异性DNA、非特异性DNA或DNA上蛋白伙伴相互作用的群体进行卷积的结果。已知二聚化能增加接触点，有助于蛋白单体稳定结合DNA。然而，我们在此表明，二聚化也可能损害靶序列上的测量停留时间和占据率，因为群体在DNA上重新分布。我们结合蛋白质与DNA之间成对可逆反应的空间随机模拟、质量作用动力学模型和理论，来分离可逆二聚化对观察到的DNA停留时间、占据率及蛋白质在DNA上空间分布的影响。三个关键主题浮现：（i）蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用，除蛋白质-DNA相互作用外，可将蛋白质定位到DNA上，因此（解）结合速率可广泛调节停留时间。（ii）通过非特异性结合和随后的1D扩散实现的维度降低，控制增强的数量级，尽管存在核小体屏障。（iii）二聚化增强对局部聚集靶标的选择性，并常通过隔离作用损害对间隔较远靶标的结合。与ChIP-seq数据相比，我们的模型解释了必需GAGA因子单体在整个基因组中的分布如何因蛋白质相互作用而对聚集靶标高度选择。该模型框架预测，即使弱二聚化也能在转录过程中重新分布和稳定DNA上的蛋白质，作为必要组成部分。
